target_customer: Adults and aspiring founders who want to learn to code and build a startup quickly, paying per course
problem: People with startup ideas could not find developers and found broad coding curricula too slow or unfocused to build a specific product.
business_model: Paid online courses (49.95 dollars per month at launch) sold direct and through Skillshare
product_category: Online coding and business skills education

founders.name: Mattan Griffel
prior_employers: Columbia Business School (faculty, later role per YC page)
education: New York University, Philosophy and Finance
founders.background_notes: No computer science training; he taught himself to code after failing to find a developer (TechCrunch 2013). YC page says he later co-founded Ophelia and was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in Education.

founders.name: Chris Castiglione
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by AlleyWatch in 2014 and listed on the YC page.

exit.reason: GoRails announced it acquired One Month and plans to revamp the site and courses; terms undisclosed.

competitors.name: Codecademy
competitors.what: Free in browser coding exercises with broad curricula

competitors.name: Learn Code The Hard Way
competitors.what: Self study coding books and lessons with broad curricula

technical_complexity.rationale: Recorded video courses on a standard website; the work was curriculum design and marketing.

defensibility.rationale: Course content was copyable by established platforms, and differentiation rested on a project based format and the founders' teaching style.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large course platforms kept competing, and One Month relied on Skillshare as a channel. The company stayed independent until GoRails acquired it in 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported over 9,000 paying students at launch in August 2013 at 49.95 dollars per month, and later coverage says its programming courses were top sellers on Skillshare.

branding.domain_note: onemonth.com is the company domain; it was reached after the One Month Rails launch name was dropped.

identity.voice_and_tone: Promise of learning a real skill in a short time, project based lessons

branding.brand_signature: The learn in one month promise

rebrands.why: AlleyWatch says it relaunched as One Month as it expanded beyond Rails to HTML/CSS and growth hacking.

branding.community_and_virality: Students published course sample apps on GitHub under omrails repositories and the courses were top sellers on Skillshare.

brand_strength.rationale: A name that states the promise, thousands of paying students and many student repositories show solid niche awareness, but it never became a category leader.

pivots.from: Single course teaching Ruby on Rails (One Month Rails)
pivots.to: Broader skills courses including HTML/CSS and growth hacking (One Month)
pivots.why: Expansion beyond one language after Skillshare sales success, per AlleyWatch.

outcome_analysis: One Month sold 49.95 dollar monthly Rails courses to over 9,000 students at launch, relaunched as a broader skills brand, raised about 2.7 million dollars of seed money in 2014 and 2015, and acquired GoRails in December 2014. It did not become a venture scale outcome and was itself acquired by GoRails in August 2025, so the YC inactive label reflects a small company that stayed alive for years rather than a clear failure.
notes: The YC directory marks One Month Inactive although the site is active and was acquired by GoRails (announcement 2025-08-14); the status conflict is explained here. The 770K seed is confirmed by a TechCrunch headline of 2014-06-25 and AlleyWatch (July 2014); investors are from AlleyWatch. The 2015 seed of 1.9M comes from AlleyWatch coverage of Griffel's statement as relayed by a search summary and I did not open the article; Startupintros lists a 2M round led by Built In LA and CB Insights lists 2.69M over 6 rounds, so totals conflict and coverage is partial. One Month also acquired GoRails around 2014-12 per VentureBeat and CB Insights. Founding year uses the YC page.
